ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance against: (i) the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List administered by Global Affairs Canada; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the OFAC SDN List for all USD-denominated Swift_TT and wire transfers; and (iv) domestic and foreign PEP databases covering Alberta provincial and Canadian federal political exposure. Screening applies continuously to all directors, shareholders with 25% or greater control, UBOs, counterparties, and beneficial owners at onboarding and on a rolling basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES – Corporate Registry Electronic System) accessed through Service Alberta-authorized Registry Agents
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A corporate name must include a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element and must be in English or French only; Chinese-language transliteration is not recognized for the legal corporate name; names must be identifiable through NUANS and must not be confusingly similar to any existing federally or provincially registered name, mark, or protected name in Canada
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banker, Trust, Loan, Assurance, Insurance (requires prior approval of Alberta Treasury Board and Finance under the Financial Institutions Act and Insurance Act)
University, College, Institute of Technology (requires prior ministerial approval under the Post-secondary Learning Act)
Engineer, Engineering, Geoscience (requires prior certification by the Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of Alberta)
Royal, Crown, Government, Municipal (requires federal or provincial Crown authorization)
Co-operative, Condominium (requires a special statute or regulatory approval)
Lawyer, Barrister, Solicitor, Notary Public (requires Law Society of Alberta approval)
Names that are obscene, scandalous, or contrary to public order, or that falsely suggest connection with a living or deceased individual
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a written Request for Reconsideration to the Director of Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the rejection notice, filed through an authorized Registry Agent, including the NUANS report, the rejected proposed name, a written legal argument, and any supporting evidence of entitlement; no statutory filing fee applies; the Director exercises discretionary review under s. 12 ABCA and a determination is normally issued within 10–15 business days; a fresh name reservation with an updated NUANS report may be filed in parallel.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable with limitations: a physical street address in Alberta (not a P.O. Box) must be designated and maintained under s. 101 ABCA; virtual office providers that receive service of process and maintain statutory corporate records are permitted for a wholesale export business (ISIC 4631), provided FINTRAC record-keeping, UBO register maintenance, and CRA correspondence obligations are fully discharged.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 5-10% risk of unannounced physical on-site verification by CRA or FINTRAC for a low-risk standard wholesale export entity; inspection likelihood increases materially if UBO disclosures are inconsistent, nominee structures are used, or the entity's registered office cannot produce required records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9; formation and governance provisions including ss. 6, 12, 14-16, 101, 106-107, 140-142.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Corporate Registries Division, Service Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation (and the statutory Certificate of Incorporation issued under the Business Corporations Act)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital; the incorporator may subscribe one or more shares without escrow. No paid-in capital deposit is required. Issued common shares are to be recorded in the corporation's securities register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Articles of Incorporation be adopted and the Certificate of Incorporation is accepted. FURTHER RESOLVED that the share structure in the Articles be ratified, and common subscription shares be issued to the initial incorporator, recorded in the securities register. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office located as specified in the Articles in Alberta is adopted as the corporation's permanent address, and corporate records shall be maintained there. FURTHER RESOLVED that the named first directors are confirmed, and they appoint a President, Secretary-Treasurer, and Chief Compliance Officer. All officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute registrations and take all lawful actions to activate the corporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Service Alberta / Alberta Corporate Registry - NUANS Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS search with the proposed legal name to assess similarity with existing corporate names and trademarks. The name must include a legal element such as Inc., Corp., Ltd., or Ltd. Reserve the name for 90 days if confirmation required, then retain the NUANS report for filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NUANS report flags a conflicting name, submit an amended name with a written explanation, or obtain a consent and undertaking from the holder of the similar name, then resubmit the search and incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Articles of Incorporation and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry - Corporate Registries Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 under the Business Corporations Act, selecting the authorized share structure, registered office address within Alberta, first directors, and any permitted share-transfer restrictions. Each first director must execute a Consent to Act as Director. No minimum capital or escrow certification is required.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as First Director for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or rejection letter, correct the identified deficiencies in the Articles and file an amended Form 1 together with a covering response letter indicating the clarifications made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Corporate Access secure e-filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Form 1 and consents electronically through Corporate Access or by paper to the Edmonton registry. Pay the CAD filing fee. Once data is validated, the registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation, at which time the corporation acquires legal personality and the registered office is established.
required_dossiers: Payment receipt (CAD 150 equivalent conversion may apply)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried after submission, respond through the portal with corrected data and supporting declarations. Where a certificate is issued with an accidental typographical error, request a certificate correction from the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Organization: Initial Board Resolution, By-Laws and Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational board meeting. Adopt by-law 1 respecting directors, officers, banking, records and corporate seal, approve the subscription for common shares by the incorporator, issue share certificates, appoint officers, select the registered office address and record all entries in the statutory registers.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the First Organizational Board Meeting
Registers of directors, officers and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer appointment fails for quorum or qualification reasons, hold a new meeting and record a ratification resolution; file any director change notice with the Alberta Corporate Registry within the applicable statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number, Provincial and Municipal Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration; Municipal Business Licensing Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online to the CRA for a Business Number and program accounts (GST/HST, payroll, import/export, or corporate income tax as needed). Register for relevant Alberta provincial tax accounts and obtain a municipal business licence using the Certificate of Incorporation and registered office particulars. Confirm whether a medical/herbal product export licence is triggered under Health Canada or CFIA.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and officer list
Lease or ownership evidence of the Alberta business premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or municipal authorities require additional business details, provide the corporation's by-law, board resolution and premises lease. If the application is denied for zoning reasons, apply for a variance or select a compliant location and update the registered office immediately.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) - Safe Food for Canadians Act/Regulations licensing division; Alberta Agriculture and Irrigation for agri-food facility registration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Safe Food for Canadians (SFC) Licence for food processing/wholesale and export; municipal business licence; CFIA organic certification for organic dried Lycium if organic label is used

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas, in coordination with Environment and Climate Change Canada
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration/Exemption category - no full Environmental Impact Assessment required for a low-impact drying, sorting, packaging and warehousing operation; Alberta Activities Designation Regulation screening applies where waste or effluent discharge thresholds are exceeded
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to municipal sewer must comply with pH 6.0-9.0, total suspended solids limits and local sewer-use by-laws; VOC and odour emissions from drying must remain below Alberta ambient air quality objectives; particulate and botanical dust emissions must be controlled by filtration and housekeeping; packaging waste handling must meet Alberta Recycling Regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire marshal inspection and fire safety certificate for the facility, structural load certification for storage racking and mezzanines, building occupancy permit from municipal development authority, and Alberta OHS clearance incl. WHMIS, dust/air exposure controls and an emergency response plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — central administrator of federal corporate income tax and federal GST/HST; Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) — provincial corporate registration and extraprovincial licence; tax filing portal: CRA My Business Account / Business Registration Online.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada or making taxable supplies in Canada must register with the CRA. Procedure: (1) obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) via Business Registration Online (BRO) using Form RC1 or RC2; (2) activate the GST/HST program account ('RT') and, if applicable, the corporate income tax account ('RC'); (3) when registering in Alberta, file an extraprovincial registration or Articles of Incorporation with the Alberta Corporate Registry and obtain the Alberta corporation number; (4) appoint a resident agent for service where required. Canada does not operate a separate VAT ID registry; the CRA BN plus RT account code serves as the GST/HST registration number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Canadian-resident corporation taxed on worldwide income; non-resident corporation taxed only on Canadian-source business income and certain capital gains; GST/HST operates at entity level and is not a pass-through tax)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box regime. Available statutory elections relevant to this structure include: GST/HST election for closely related corporations under ETA s. 156, quick-method election for certain GST/HST registrants, and non-resident elections under Income Tax Act s. 216 for net-basis tax on Canadian rental/royalty income; s. 219 branch tax applies automatically to non-resident corporations. Hybrid mismatch rules under ss. 18.4, 18.5, 94, 94.1, 94.2, and 94.3 do not permit elective recharacterization of an entity's tax status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) — Alberta has no provincial sales tax; federal GST applies at 5%; exported commercial goods are zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated exports) over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; voluntary registration is available to exporters seeking to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory e-invoicing approval system exists in Canada. GST/HST invoices must contain CRA-required particulars, including supplier name, GST/HST registration number, invoice date, description of goods, amount, tax rate, and tax collected; electronic invoices are permissible if legible and accessible to the CRA. Export documentation is transmitted electronically to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS), not through a tax-authority clearance engine.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Dried goji berries and herbal botanicals are zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act when the supplier: (i) exports the goods directly from Canada; (ii) ships them to a destination outside Canada; or (iii) delivers them to a common carrier for export within a reasonable time. The exporter must maintain documentary evidence proving physical export, such as transport documents, CBSA export declarations, freight bills, and destination-country import records. Because the supply is taxable at 0% rather than exempt, the exporter may claim input tax credits for GST paid on acquisitions related to the export business.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Form B13A / B13B Export Declaration filed via the CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) or automated export declaration portal
Commercial invoice showing exporter, foreign buyer, description, quantity, HS code 0813.40 for dried goji berries, and value in Canadian dollars
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (or Cargo Control Document / PARS highway equivalent) evidencing dispatch to the foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank payment advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the foreign buyer
Certificate of origin and phytosanitary inspection records where required for herbal botanical imports in the destination jurisdiction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reverse a zero-rating treatment, disallow related input tax credits, and reassess GST/HST plus interest where the exporter cannot substantiate physical export within the statutory record-retention period (six years). False statements or misrepresentations attract penalties under Excise Tax Act ss. 280(1)-(2) (5% immediate penalty plus 1% per month on unremitted amounts) and Income Tax Act s. 163(2) (50% of the additional tax for gross negligence); fraudulent export claims may also attract criminal prosecution. Canada imposes no formal foreign-exchange repatriation statute, but receipt of export proceeds within 180 days and preservation of bank remittance records are the practical audit benchmark; failure to collect does not alone trigger clawback if genuine export is established, although missing payment evidence materially weakens the export-credibility review.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Functional supervision is distributed across OSFI (prudential regulation of banks and insurance), Global Affairs Canada (export controls under the Export and Import Permits Act), FINTRAC (AML/CFT monitoring of cross-border electronic funds transfers under the PCMLTFA), and Payments Canada (clearing and settlement rail ownership, including Lynx).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Canada has accepted Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement and imposes no exchange-control licensing, no capital-repatriation approval, and no restriction on dividend remittance, loan servicing, or share-capital restitution for an Alberta business corporation. Residual frictions are non-FX in nature: Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties; FINTRAC reporting of electronic funds transfers at or above CAD 10,000; and bank-level KYC/AML evidentiary requirements triggered by non-resident beneficial ownership.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender, conversion, or repatriation requirement on export proceeds and prescribes no mandatory timeline for collection of foreign receivables. The exporter may hold any currency balance in Canada or abroad. Compliance obligations are limited to routine FINTRAC reporting of EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more, CBSA export documentation where required, and accurate inclusion of foreign-currency revenue in taxable income under the Income Tax Act, using either the transactional or functional-currency translation rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with dual CAD/USD treasury module
Operational Account with dedicated trade finance and LC desk
Operational Account / USD clearing through US correspondent rail
Operational Account with Asia-Pacific and Latin America correspondent network
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (Alberta provincial Crown institution)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — limited. The European EMI designation has no direct statutory analogue under Canadian law; digital payment providers operating in Canada are regulated as Money Service Businesses (MSBs) and must register with FINTRAC. Platforms such as Wise, Airwallex, and Payoneer are workable as secondary rails for mid-value operational settlement, multi-currency concentration, and automated reconciliation, but they cannot issue commercial letters of credit, act as reimbursing banks under MT700, or provide documentary trade finance. They must therefore complement, not replace, a Schedule I chartered bank as the primary clearing counterparty for bulk agricultural export flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is generally permitted for directors of federal and Alberta business corporations through digital identity verification, credit-bureau corroboration, and notarized or commissioner-oath corporate resolutions. No statutory requirement mandates physical branch attendance; however, banks routinely require a live video interview of authorized signatories for USD-denominated accounts, for non-resident UBOs, or where the entity is newly formed and lacks a historical banking footprint. Planning recommendation: arrange one structured video interview per signatory, keep apostilled registry extracts ready, and expect a wet-ink corporate-mandate document when opening the USD module or when banking with ATB Financial.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated Alberta Business Corporation with no operating history, no local employees, and non-resident ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Articles of Incorporation and current Alberta registry extract; registered-office address proof (lease or service-agreement); completed schedule of beneficial ownership; passport and proof-of-address for each director and all 10%+ shareholders; apostilled corporate registry extracts of foreign parent entities; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements for each non-resident subscriber.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High projected wire turnover from dried-goji and herbal wholesale transactions that is disproportionate to declared share capital and tangible assets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed export contracts and pro forma invoices incorporating Incoterms 2020; purchase orders from downstream food, beverage, or botanical-extract buyers; third-party warehouse and logistics agreements; upstream supplier contracts with inland freight documentation; CBSA export declarations; a board-approved cash-flow forecast reconciling projected turnover with available working capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: USD wire frequency to jurisdictions perceived as correspondent-banking risk or where the goji product has ambiguous food-versus-herbal classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of historical bank statements where available; entity-level KYC files and legal-entity identifiers for the ten largest counterparties; organic, HACCP, and ISO certification dossiers with certifying-body details; laboratory certificates of analysis per lot; a written CFIA classification note and a tariff-classification memorandum resolving whether the good is dried fruit (HS 0813.40) or a herbal/pharmaceutical input (HS 1211.90).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-controlled capital structure carrying intercompany shareholder loans that attract additional bank tax-transparency screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share register and register of transfers; by-laws and unanimous shareholder agreement; intercompany loan agreements with promissory notes and arm's-length interest support; foreign registry extracts with apostilles; parent-company source-of-funds letter backed by audited financial statements; Alberta statutory address and named agent confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Operation conducted through a third-party management-office address with no physical Alberta facility or dedicated staffing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Management-office service agreement; landlord letter or utility bill evidencing the registered office; commodity-flow map from supplier farm gate or consolidation warehouse to bill-of-lading; evidence of third-party quality inspection arrangements; written AML attestation confirming absence of Politically Exposed Persons and no sanctions-list intersections.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity subscriptions and shareholder loans arrive via SWIFT MT103 or internal bank wire. Instruction fields must carry the beneficiary legal name, institution number, transit number, account number, and a purpose narration such as 'Equity Injection - Share Subscription' or 'Shareholder Loan Disbursement'. No exchange-control approval or government purpose-code declaration is required because both current and capital account payments are unrestricted in Canada. The receiving financial institution automatically reports EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC. For smooth clearing, the remitter should reference the receiving bank's direct-clearing BIC (e.g., ROYCCAT2, TDOMCATTTOR, BOFMCAT2) and keep the beneficiary address in the field-50K/59 block. Equity injections must be documented by board resolution and share subscription, and intercompany loans by demand promissory note, so that the legal characterization supports the tax treatment under the Income Tax Act and prevents reclassification of the injection as foreign business income.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements are executed on three principal rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for open-account telegraphic transfers, including GPI with a Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference (UETR) for real-time tracking; (ii) MT202COV for USD reimbursement legs where clearing passes through US Fedwire or CHIPS correspondents; and (iii) documentary trade instruments, namely commercial letters of credit (MT700 issuance, MT707 amendment, MT754/MT799 advice, MT756 settlement claim) and documentary collections (MT400/MT410), used when counterparties require LC security. CAD leg clearing runs on Lynx, Payments Canada's real-time gross settlement system, with immediate finality; USD legs clear through the Canadian bank's US correspondent account network. Each outbound instruction should be reconciled against the governing sales invoice and packing list to produce an auditable trail satisfying CRA, IFRS 15, and bank trade-compliance review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD foreign-exchange forwards (plain vanilla) with tenors up to 24 months, permitted under OSFI guidance when functionally matched to forecast trade receivables from bulk goji-berry shipments.
FX swaps (simultaneous spot and forward legs) for short-term USD liquidity management and conversion-cycle smoothing.
Cross-currency basis swaps for structural hedging of multi-year USD-denominated trade receivable or financing exposure on the Alberta balance sheet.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) — legally permissible under Canadian common law but commercially uncommon against CAD given full convertibility; defensible exclusively where a distinctive-currency fixing (for example CNH/CAD or CNY-linked invoicing) is required to hedge the underlying settlement mismatch.

Purchased European-style FX options (single-premium, non-speculative) providing protective floors on major bulk shipment receivables without exposing the treasury to unlimited mark-to-market liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Service Alberta - Corporate Registry (Registrar of Corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following each incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 50 late filing penalty if filed after the 60-day window; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative dissolution (strike-off) by the Registrar without a court proceeding.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and Alberta AT1 Corporate Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); Alberta Treasury Board and Finance - Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; balance of tax due no later than 3 months after year-end for Canadian-controlled private corporations; instalments due monthly during the year when applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeated non-compliance attracts a 10% repeated-failure penalty, prescribed interest, enforcement garnishment, loss of export-related tax clearance, and director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and delivery of annual financial statements to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; reviewed by Service Alberta Corporate Registry upon inspection or shareholder complaint
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM held no later than 15 months after the previous AGM and in every calendar year; financial statements delivered at least 21 days before the meeting date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: ABCA non-compliance offence; a shareholder or director may apply for a court compliance order; sustained delinquency alongside a late or missing annual return increases administrative strike-off risk and exposes directors to personal civil liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and reconciliation of the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register) and share transfer journal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office in Alberta; available for inspection by Service Alberta Corporate Registry and enforcement agencies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Register updated within 15 days after any change in significant control; full confirmation completed at each annual return anniversary and before any share transfer is recorded
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory offence liability for directors and officers; false or incomplete entries invalidate reliance on the register in legal or regulatory proceedings and support a registry compliance audit or escalated strike-off review.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue, asset, or headcount threshold under the Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA). A licensed independent auditor is mandatory unless a private non-distributing corporation renews an annual unanimous shareholder resolution waiving the audit; distributing or public corporations, CRA-issued audit requirements, and lender or export-financing covenants require a certified audit regardless of corporate size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for distributing or public corporations; ASPE (Canadian private-enterprise GAAP, CPA Canada Handbook Part II) permitted for private wholesale exporters; T2 reconciliation follows the elected reporting framework and CRA prescribed forms.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under ABCA Part 6.1, the corporation must maintain a current Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register) at its Alberta registered office, listing every individual with 25% or more of voting shares or share value, or with de facto control. The register must be amended within 15 days of any transfer or change, and the directors must confirm its accuracy at the annual return filing point; each share transfer must be logged in the transfer journal with transferor and transferee particulars and cross-referenced to the ISC Register before the annual confirmation can be certified.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register)
Share Transfer Register and Transfer Journal

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 if unanimous audit waiver renewed annually; 4,000-12,000 for a licensed independent audit of a small wholesale exporter

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) Small Business Deduction reduces the combined federal-Alberta rate to 11% (federal 9% + Alberta 2%) on the first C$500,000 of active business income; SBD is progressively clawed back where taxable capital exceeds C$10M and is eliminated at C$15M. Manufacturing and processing profits may qualify for a reduced federal rate of 13%. SR&ED refundable investment tax credits and various provincial credits are available. Non-resident-controlled corporations are excluded from the SBD and pay the general 23% rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal) with integrated Alberta corporate income tax administered by the Canada Revenue Agency; e-filed through CRA-certified tax preparation software via the CRA 'My Business Account' portal or an authorised EFILE service provider.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within six months after the corporation's fiscal period end (e.g., 30 June for a 31 December year-end); any balance of tax due must be paid within three months after year-end for a CCPC or two months after year-end for a non-CCPC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, Business Number (BN), fiscal year-end date, registered office address, and jurisdiction of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Canadian permanent establishment address and CRA-assigned BN; identify the country of tax residence in the treaty exposure fields.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Year-end total assets, liabilities, issued share capital, retained earnings, and shareholders' equity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the Canadian permanent establishment balance sheet; keep home-office capital and foreign subsidiary balances separate and arm's-length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue, operating expenses, and net income before taxes of the Canadian wholesale business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Canadian-source income attributable to the Alberta permanent establishment; exclude foreign-source sales documentation and revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening inventory, purchases, direct material and labour, closing inventory for the dried goji berry and herbal botanicals wholesale operation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Inventory physically located in Canada must be supported by warehouse records; intercompany inventory transfers must be valued at arm's-length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1 – Federal Part I Tax Calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal Part I tax at 15% general or 9% SBD rate on qualifying active business income; includes taxable capital, investment tax credits, and refundable tax calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-controlled corporation is not a CCPC and must compute Part I tax at the full 15% rate; apply treaty relief only through the applicable DTA forms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 5 – Province of Filing and Permanent Establishment Allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determines the province of filing and allocates taxable income among provinces based on permanent establishment gross revenue and wages.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation is subject to Alberta tax only if it maintains a permanent establishment in Alberta; otherwise allocate income to the province where a PE exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta corporate income tax at 8% general rate or 2% SBD rate on the Alberta-allocated taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute Alberta tax on the allocated PE income; where no Alberta PE exists, the line is zero and the corporation files in the province of its PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form T106 – Summary of Transactions with Non-Arm's-Length Persons
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory disclosure of each non-arm's-length cross-border transaction with a non-resident where the annual aggregate exceeds C$1 million.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File even where a tax treaty exempts business profits; failure to file attracts a C$2,500 penalty and may trigger a transfer-pricing audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of the unpaid tax balance plus 1% per full month of lateness up to 12 months; repeat filing failure: 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months; daily compounded interest at the CRA prescribed quarterly rate plus 4 percentage points; C$2,500 penalty per late or missing T106; directors may be personally assessed for unremitted source deductions under s. 227.1.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Part XIII of the Income Tax Act) on the gross amount of dividends paid or credited to a non-resident shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must obtain an official Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the home tax authority and submit Form NR303 – 'Application for a Reduction in the Amount of Non-Resident Tax Withheld' to the CRA before payment; the Canadian payer retains the NR303, TRC, and shareholding evidence. Under the Canada-China Income Tax Agreement, a Chinese corporate shareholder holding at least 10% of the voting power attracts a 5% dividend rate (15% otherwise); the reduced rate applies only after the forms are filed and accepted.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT: royalties 25%, interest 25%. Treaty rates: Canada-China DTA – royalties 10%, interest 10%; Canada-US Treaty – royalties generally 10% (certain copyright royalties 15%), interest generally 0% on arm's-length and qualifying bank debt; Canada-UK DTA – royalties 10%, interest 0% in most cases.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Form T106 and transfer-pricing documentation are mandatory where the total annual value of non-arm's-length cross-border transactions exceeds C$1,000,000; local file and master file content must be made available within 3 months (6 months for master file) of a CRA demand; Country-by-Country reporting is required for MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least C$750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not administer formal Economic Substance Regulations; instead, economic substance is enforced through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (ITA s. 245), the common-law sham and substance-over-form doctrines, and the 'central management and control' residency test. Transactions lacking commercial rationality or genuine business purpose may be recharacterised, denied tax benefits, and subjected to gross-negligence penalties.
